text: Designs, develops, and maintains production software systems in Malaysia's digital economy corridor. Writes modular Python scripts, integrates RESTful APIs and webhook microservices, queries SQL relational databases, and deploys containerised backend applications.

Builds enterprise knowledge retrieval systems using large language models, vector databases, semantic search embeddings, and structured prompt engineering. Implements REST APIs, Python data ingestion scripts, and human-in-the-loop hallucination guardrails.

Evaluates enterprise standard operating procedures and performs business process mapping across Malaysian shared services centres. Designs automated multi-step agentic workflows, integrates REST APIs, and establishes human-in-the-loop quality review checkpoints.

Leads workplace generative AI deployment by mapping business process bottlenecks, authoring structured prompt templates, orchestrating workflow automation pipelines, and communicating KPI impact to management stakeholders.

Manages enterprise relational databases, writes complex SQL queries and data warehouse transformations, enforces Malaysia Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA 2010) access controls, and builds executive KPI dashboards.

Curates structured SQL data marts and unstructured document indexing pipelines for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Writes Python ETL scripts, connects REST API endpoints, and enforces PDPA data governance rules.

Prepares corporate sustainability disclosures aligned with Bursa Malaysia Main Market ESG guidelines and ISSB standards. Conducts Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 carbon footprint analytics, SQL emissions data analysis, and executive data visualization.

Audits enterprise AI systems against Malaysia MOSTI National AI Governance and Ethics (AIGE) guidelines and Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA 2010). Conducts algorithmic bias assessments, human-in-the-loop oversight checks, and stakeholder policy briefings.

Designs adult reskilling curricula and HRD Corp e-LATiH training modules on foundational AI literacy, structured prompt engineering, and workplace workflow transformation. Facilitates stakeholder change management across departments.
Performs routine clerical duties including photocopying forms, sorting physical mail, filing paper invoices in cabinets, and manual typing of standard letters without digital automation software.
Manually keys handwritten receipts, paper survey forms, and shipping dockets into static spreadsheets. Performs repetitive copy-paste transcription without SQL queries or workflow automation tools.

Coordinates departmental schedules, documents standard operating procedures and business process maps, and communicates project updates across stakeholders while beginning foundational AI literacy training.

source: Public Competency Framework (AI Untuk Rakyat (MyDIGITAL & MDEC National Self-Paced Programme) / Elements of AI)
text: Foundational AI Literacy & LLM Capabilities (AI Core): Understand generative AI capabilities, hallucination limits, and safe workplace usage. Demonstrated proficiency in artificial intelligence, large language model, llm, generative ai.

source: Public Competency Framework (Skill Objective: Structured Prompt & Rubric Design (HRD Corp e-LATiH / Open Documentation))
text: Structured Prompting & Context Engineering (AI Core): Design reproducible, schema-constrained prompts with explicit verification rubrics. Demonstrated proficiency in prompt, in-context learning, context engineering, instruction tuning.

source: Public Competency Framework (Skill Objective: Operational Workflow Mapping & Bottleneck Analysis (e-LATiH))
text: Business Process Mapping & SOP Design (Operations): Deconstruct manual workplace workflows into auditable human vs. AI-assisted steps. Demonstrated proficiency in business process, workflow, process mining, sop.

source: Public Competency Framework (PostgreSQL / SQLite Official Documentation & Interactive SQL Exercises)
text: SQL & Structured Data Analysis (Data & Engineering): Query relational datasets, audit missing values, and validate KPI baselines reproducibly. Demonstrated proficiency in sql, database, tabular data, text-to-sql.

source: Public Competency Framework (Official Python 3 Tutorial & Standard Library Reference)
text: Python Scripting & Data Automation (Data & Engineering): Write modular Python scripts for data validation, API requests, and automated testing. Demonstrated proficiency in python, scripting, code generation, software engineering.

source: Public Competency Framework (Skill Objective: Evidence-Based Dashboard & Uncertainty Reporting)
text: Data Visualization & KPI Storytelling (Operations): Communicate uncertainty intervals, baselines, and operational KPIs clearly to stakeholders. Demonstrated proficiency in data visualization, visualization, dashboard, dashboards.

source: Public Competency Framework (Skill Objective: Human-in-the-Loop AI Workflow Orchestration & Fallback Design)
text: Agentic Workflow Orchestration & Tool Integration (AI Core): Chain bounded AI tool calls with deterministic fallback and human approval checkpoints. Demonstrated proficiency in agentic, ai agent, ai agents, llm agent.

source: Public Competency Framework (NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) — Measure & Verify Playbook)
text: Human-in-the-Loop Evaluation & AI Testing (Governance & QA): Build gold-standard evaluation sets, detect AI hallucinations, and enforce guardrails. Demonstrated proficiency in llm evaluation, model evaluation, hallucination, hallucinations.

source: Public Competency Framework (Skill Objective: Source-Grounded Retrieval & Citation Verification Pipeline)
text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) & Citation Grounding (Data & Engineering): Index dated organizational documents and enforce strict source-citation grounding. Demonstrated proficiency in retrieval-augmented, retrieval augmented, rag, vector database.

source: Public Competency Framework (MDN Web Docs — HTTP & REST API Architecture Guides)
text: REST API Integration & Resilient Fallbacks (Data & Engineering): Integrate external JSON/XML data feeds with schema validation, timeouts, and snapshot fallbacks. Demonstrated proficiency in api, apis, rest api, endpoint.

source: Public Competency Framework (Malaysia National Guidelines on AI Governance & Ethics (MOSTI) & UNESCO AI Ethics)
text: AI Ethics, Fairness Auditing & Governance (Governance & QA): Audit AI systems for demographic fairness, transparency, and compliance with Malaysia's National Guidelines on AI Governance & Ethics (AIGE). Demonstrated proficiency in ai ethics, ethics, fairness, algorithmic bias.

source: Public Competency Framework (OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications & PDPA Compliance Objective)
text: Data Privacy & Malaysian PDPA Compliance (Governance & QA): Apply data minimization, synthetic test profiling, and Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) controls. Demonstrated proficiency in privacy, pdpa, personal data, anonymization.

source: Public Competency Framework (UN CC:e-Learn (United Nations Climate Change Learning Partnership) Free Courses)
text: ESG Frameworks & UN SDG Impact Mapping (Sustainability): Map operational and digital initiatives to UN SDG targets and quantifiable sustainability KPIs. Demonstrated proficiency in sustainability, sdg, sdgs, climate.

source: Public Competency Framework (Green Software Foundation — Green Software Practitioner (Free Linux Foundation Course))
text: Carbon-Aware Compute & Resource Telemetry (Sustainability): Measure compute energy efficiency and right-size AI workloads (CPU vs. GPU). Demonstrated proficiency in carbon, carbon footprint, energy consumption, energy efficiency.

source: Public Competency Framework (Skill Objective: Human-Centred AI Change Management & Advisory Communication)
text: Human-Centred Change & Stakeholder Communication (Operations): Facilitate human-in-charge career and operational decisions alongside AI recommendations. Demonstrated proficiency in stakeholder, stakeholders, human-centered, human-centred.

source: Public Competency Framework (UNESCO-UNEVOC TVET & Digital Competency Frameworks (Open Resource))
text: Competency Matrix & Reskilling Curriculum Design (Operations): Structure modular adult reskilling pathways mapped to Malaysia's TVET and HRD Corp frameworks. Demonstrated proficiency in curriculum, reskilling, upskilling, workforce training.

Occupation: embedded systems software developer. Embedded systems software developers program, implement, document and maintain software to be run on an embedded system. Core tasks and competencies: develop software prototype; integrated development environment software; provide technical documentation; utilise computer-aided software engineering tools; ICT debugging tools; debug software; use software design patterns; interpret technical texts; use software libraries; Internet of Things. Supplementary skills: Prolog (computer programming); R; object-oriented modelling; Jenkins (tools for software configuration management); VBScript.

Occupation: industrial mobile devices software developer. Industrial mobile devices software developers implement applications software for specific, professional industrial mobile (handheld) devices, based on the industry needs, using general or specific development tools for device operating systems. Core tasks and competencies: mobile operating systems; use software design patterns; integrated development environment software; create flowchart diagram; use software libraries; develop software prototype; interpret technical texts; analyse software specifications; computer programming; use different communication channels. Supplementary skills: R; Android (mobile operating systems); Scala; Scratch (computer programming); use functional programming.

Occupation: ICT application developer. ICT application developers implement the ICT (software) applications based on the designs provided using application domain specific languages, tools, platforms and experience. Core tasks and competencies: utilise computer-aided software engineering tools; propose ICT solutions to business problems; create flowchart diagram; provide technical documentation; develop automated migration methods; computer programming; interpret technical texts; service-oriented modelling; manage business knowledge; integrated development environment software. Supplementary skills: object-oriented modelling; Puppet (tools for software configuration management); software anomalies; VBScript; Common Lisp.

Occupation: data analyst. Data analysts import, inspect, clean, transform, validate, model, or interpret collections of data with regard to the business goals of the company. They ensure that the data sources and repositories provide consistent and reliable data. Data analysts use different algorithms and IT tools as demanded by the situation and the current data. They might prepare reports in the form of visualisations such as graphs, charts, and dashboards. Core tasks and competencies: information confidentiality; establish data processes; execute analytical mathematical calculations; collect ICT data; business intelligence; normalise data; integrate ICT data; interpret current data; handle data samples; visual presentation techniques. Supplementary skills: SPARQL; cloud technologies; database; create data models; gather data for forensic purposes.

Occupation: call centre analyst. Call centre analysts examine data regarding incoming or outgoing customer calls. They prepare reports and visualisation. Core tasks and competencies: run simulations; analyse call centre activities; train staff on call quality assurance; gather data; inspect data; call quality assurance management; analyse call performance trends; apply numeracy skills; create solutions to problems; report call errors. Supplementary skills: report accounts of the professional activity; information confidentiality; teamwork principles; deliver visual presentation of data; ensure compliance with company regulations.

Occupation: meter reader. Meter readers visit residential and business or industrial buildings and facilities in order to note down the readings of the meters which measure gas, water, electricity and other utility uses. They forward the results to the client and to the supplier. Core tasks and competencies: report utility meter readings; operate GPS systems; mathematics; read water meter; road traffic laws; read gas meter; identify faults in utility meters; interpret traffic signals; inspect for unauthorised connections; recognise signs of corrosion. Supplementary skills: monitor utility equipment; read heat meter; gas consumption; operate electronic measuring instruments; advise on utility consumption.

Occupation: securities analyst. Securities analysts perform research activities to gather and analyse financial, legal and economic information. They interpret data on the price, stability and future investment trends in a certain economic area and make recommendations and forecasts to business clients. Core tasks and competencies: securities; investment analysis; collect financial data; financial products; review investment portfolios; develop investment portfolio; analyse market financial trends; analyse financial risk; actuarial science; financial markets. Supplementary skills: banking activities; liaise with managers; statistics; provide cost benefit analysis reports; perform stock valuation.

Occupation: data scientist. Data scientists find and interpret rich data sources, manage large amounts of data, merge data sources, ensure consistency of data-sets, and create visualisations to aid in understanding data. They build mathematical models using data, present and communicate data insights and findings to specialists and scientists in their team and if required, to a non-expert audience, and recommend ways to apply the data. Core tasks and competencies: execute analytical mathematical calculations; statistics; interpret current data; information extraction; deliver visual presentation of data; collect ICT data; build recommender systems; implement data quality processes; normalise data; manage data collection systems. Supplementary skills: manage ICT data architecture; data quality assessment; LINQ; manage ICT data classification; XQuery.

Occupation: knowledge engineer. Knowledge engineers integrate structured knowledge into computer systems (knowledge bases) in order to solve complex problems normally requiring a high level of human expertise or artificial intelligence methods. They are also responsible for eliciting or extracting knowledge from information sources, maintaining this knowledge, and making it available to the organisation or users. To achieve this, they are aware of knowledge representation and maintenance techniques (rules, frames, semantic nets, ontologies) and use knowledge extraction techniques and tools. They can design and build expert or artificial intelligence systems that use this knowledge. Core tasks and competencies: resource description framework query language; web programming; use markup languages; natural language processing; database development tools; manage database; define technical requirements; business process modelling; task algorithmisation; manage business knowledge. Supplementary skills: Haskell; computer programming; Objective-C; CoffeeScript; Swift (computer programming).

Occupation: instrumentation engineer. Instrumentation engineers envision and design equipment used in manufacturing processes for controlling and monitoring various engineering processes remotely. They design equipment for the monitoring of production sites such as manufacturing systems, machinery uses and production processes. Core tasks and competencies: environmental threats; abide by regulations on banned materials; instrumentation equipment; environmental legislation; design drawings; physics; control systems; approve engineering design; perform scientific research; engineering principles. Supplementary skills: record test data; ensure equipment availability; nuclear energy; use technical drawing software; manage system testing.

Occupation: packing machinery engineer. Packing machinery engineers are in charge of and responsible for packaging machinery. They maintain and improve technical standards, analyse results, set up improvement plans, and are responsible for machinery maintenance. Core tasks and competencies: read engineering drawings; troubleshoot; industrial engineering; mechanical engineering; types of packaging materials; CAD software; use technical drawing software; provide technical documentation; engineering principles; adjust engineering designs. Supplementary skills: determine production feasibility; provide advice to technicians; blueprints; use CAM software; set up the controller of a machine.

Occupation: equipment engineer. Equipment engineers design and maintain the machinery and equipment in manufacturing facilities. They design machinery that adjusts to the manufacturing requirements and processes. Moreover, they envision the maintenance of the machines and equipment for uninterrupted functioning. 
 Core tasks and competencies: engineering processes; use technical drawing software; define technical requirements; manufacturing processes; interpret technical requirements; execute analytical mathematical calculations; engineering principles; project management; production processes; perform scientific research. Supplementary skills: design prototypes; inspect industrial equipment; record test data; use CAD software; design principles.

Occupation: paper engineer. Paper engineers ensure an optimal production process in the manufacture of paper and related products. They select primary and secondary raw materials and check their quality. In addition, they optimize machinery and equipment usage as well as the chemical additives for paper making. Core tasks and competencies: types of paper; check quality of raw materials; types of pulp; paper production processes; perform scientific research; test paper production samples; sizes of paper; engineering processes; check paper quality; paper chemistry. Supplementary skills: identify hazards in the workplace; perform project management; communication; prepare production reports; types of wood.

Occupation: ICT system administrator. ICT system administrators are responsible for the upkeep, configuration, and reliable operation of computer and network systems, servers, workstations and peripheral devices. They may acquire, install, or upgrade computer components and software; automate routine tasks; write computer programs; troubleshoot; train and supervise staff; and provide technical support. They ensure optimum system integrity, security, backup and performance. Core tasks and competencies: implement ICT recovery system; support ICT system users; perform backups; organisational policies; interpret technical texts; solve ICT system problems; ICT infrastructure; software components libraries; ICT system programming; apply system organisational policies. Supplementary skills: ICT recovery techniques; interact with users to gather requirements; interfacing techniques; engineering processes; ICT system integration.

Occupation: ICT security administrator. ICT security administrators plan and carry out security measures to protect information and data from unauthorised access, deliberate attack, theft and corruption. Core tasks and competencies: maintain database security; solve ICT system problems; quality assurance methodologies; Internet of Things; perform ICT troubleshooting; internet governance; apply company policies; organisational resilience; maintain ICT identity management; manage IT security compliances. Supplementary skills: address problems critically; train employees; ICT security standards; use scripting programming; perform backups.

Occupation: telecommunications engineering technician. Telecommunications engineering technician deploy, maintain and monitor a telecommunication system that provides interactions between data and voice communications, such as telephone, video conferencing, computer, and voicemail systems. They are also involved in the design, manufacturing, construction, maintenance and repair of telecommunication systems. Telecommunications engineering technicians provide technical assistance in the research and development of telecommunication equipment. Core tasks and competencies: interpret technical texts; microwave principles; apply system organisational policies; apply ICT system usage policies; manage changes in ICT system; electronics principles; upgrade firmware; analog electronics theory; organisational policies; operate electronic measuring instruments. Supplementary skills: Perl; Python (computer programming); Erlang; solve ICT system problems; OpenEdge Advanced Business Language.

Occupation: education administrator. Education administrators organise and manage the administration, support systems and (student) activities of an education institution. They perform a range of administrative, secretarial, financial and otherwise supportive tasks to enable the efficient and cost-effective running of the school. They may assist in student recruitment, alumni relations, funding, work on committees including academic boards and quality insurance. Core tasks and competencies: electronic communication; manage budgets; maintain records of financial transactions; customer service; trace financial transactions; manage educational institution's administration; budgetary principles; office software; handle financial transactions; education administration. Supplementary skills: cooperate with education professionals; use different communication channels; deliver correspondence; use office systems; kindergarten school procedures.

Occupation: secretary. 
Secretaries perform a variety of administrative tasks to help keep an organisation run smoothly. They answer telephone calls, draft and send e-mails, maintain diaries, arrange appointments, take messages, file documents, organise and service meetings, and manage databases. Core tasks and competencies: handle mail; communicate by telephone; perform office routine activities; company policies; draft corporate emails; communicate schedules to the people concerned; monitor staff absences; process commissioned instructions; manage personnel agenda; disseminate internal communications. Supplementary skills: use office systems; handle petty cash; deliver correspondence; organise travel arrangements for staff; handle financial transactions.

Occupation: database developer. Database developers program, implement and coordinate changes to computer databases based on their expertise of database management systems. Core tasks and competencies: apply information security policies; data storage; database management systems; balance database resources; query languages; resource description framework query language; data quality assessment; interpret technical texts; collect customer feedback on applications; perform backups. Supplementary skills: Ruby (computer programming); OpenEdge Database; Microsoft Access; APL; Filemaker (database management systems).

Occupation: database integrator. Database integrators perform integration among different databases. They maintain integration and ensure interoperability. Core tasks and competencies: verify formal ICT specifications; database management systems; balance database resources; execute integration testing; create database diagrams; query languages; implement data warehousing techniques; integrate ICT data; manage ICT legacy implication; ICT debugging tools. Supplementary skills: Pentaho Data Integration; Oracle Data Integrator; IBM InfoSphere DataStage; use scripting programming; IBM Informix.

Occupation: business analyst. 
Business analysts research and understand the strategic position of businesses and companies in relation to their markets and their stakeholders. They analyse and present their views on how the company, from many perspectives, can improve its strategic position and internal corporate structure. They assess needs for change, communication methods, technology, IT tools, new standards and certifications. Core tasks and competencies: perform business analysis; align efforts towards business development; conduct qualitative research; business analysis; conduct quantitative research; interpret financial statements; liaise with managers; analyse internal factors of companies; identify undetected organisational needs; build business relationships. Supplementary skills: business law; shape organisational teams based on competencies; advise on financial matters; interview people; advise on organisation climate.

Occupation: business economics researcher. Business economics researchers conduct research on topics regarding economy, organisations, and strategy. They analyse macroeconomic and microeconomic trends and use this information to analyse the positions of industries or specific companies in the economy. They provide advice regarding strategic planning, product feasibility, forecast trends, emerging markets, taxing policies, and consumer trends. Core tasks and competencies: conduct quantitative research; financial markets; apply scientific methods; forecast economic trends; execute analytical mathematical calculations; advise on economic development; analyse economic trends; apply statistical analysis techniques; business management principles; economics. Supplementary skills: analyse financial performance of a company; commercial law; monitor national economy; assess risk factors; write scientific papers.

Occupation: ICT business analyst. ICT business analysts are in charge of analysing and designing an organisation's processes and systems, assessing the business model and its integration with technology. They also identify change needs, assess the impact of the change, capture and document requirements and then ensure that these requirements are delivered whilst supporting the business through the implementation process. Core tasks and competencies: business requirements techniques; identify legal requirements; legal requirements of ICT products; analyse the context of an organisation; identify customer requirements; create business process models; interact with users to gather requirements; propose ICT solutions to business problems; apply change management; translate requirement concepts into visual design. Supplementary skills: manage ICT project; decision support systems; ICT market; visual presentation techniques; execute analytical mathematical calculations.

Occupation: ICT business analysis manager. ICT business analysis managers identify areas where information system changes are needed to support business plans and monitor the impact in terms of change management. They contribute to the general ICT functional requirements of the business organisation. ICT business analysis managers analyse business needs and translate them into ICT solutions. Core tasks and competencies: perform business analysis; decision support systems; design process; implement strategic planning; define technical requirements; manage ICT project; provide ICT consulting advice; improve business processes; provide cost benefit analysis reports; business process modelling. Supplementary skills: communicate with customers; ICT market; information extraction; execute analytical mathematical calculations; data mining.

Occupation: marketeer. Marketing consultants advise companies in the development of marketing strategies for specific purposes. They can advise and develop strategies for the entry of a brand in the market, for the re-launch of a product, for the introduction of a new product, or for the positioning of a commercial image. They perform previous studies of the position of the company and perception of customers in order to define the marketing approach. Core tasks and competencies: identify market niches; define technical requirements; use consulting techniques; maintain relationship with customers; market analysis; plan marketing strategy; respond to enquiries; marketing principles; use different communication channels; conduct research interview. Supplementary skills: customer service; make strategic business decisions; coordinate marketing plan actions; social media management; evaluate marketing content.

Occupation: online marketer. Online marketers use e-mail, internet and social media in order to market goods and brands.
 Core tasks and competencies: perform image editing; perform video editing; execute conversion testing; perform market research; implement marketing strategies; apply social media marketing; company policies; execute email marketing; manage budgets; use different communication channels. Supplementary skills: conduct search engine optimisation; competition law; adapt to change in marketing; deal with pressure from unexpected circumstances; supervise brand management.

Occupation: network marketer. Network marketers apply various marketing strategies, including ​network marketing strategies to sell products and convince new people to also join in and start selling these products. They use personal relations to attract customers and sell various types of products. Core tasks and competencies: apply strategic thinking; sell products; apply customer engagement strategy; product comprehension; advertising techniques; communication; characteristics of products; marketing principles; marketing mix; implement sales strategies. Supplementary skills: build business relationships; demonstrate products' features; public relations; identify new business opportunities; customer service.

Occupation: advertising specialist. Advertising specialists provide advice to companies and organisations about the development of their advertising strategies and on advertising-related topics covering a more general strategic approach. They combine knowledge of marketing, budgets, and psychology with a creative mind to develop advertising campaigns. They propose alternatives to clients that promote their organisations, products, or projects. Core tasks and competencies: perform market research; persuade clients with alternatives; give live presentation; brainstorm ideas; advertising techniques; develop professional network; identify customer's needs; liaise with advertising agencies; copyright legislation; develop creative ideas. Supplementary skills: marketing principles; coordinate advertising campaigns; develop public relations strategies; analyse cultural trends; types of media.

Occupation: energy consultant. Energy consultants advise clients on the advantages and disadvantages of different energy sources. They help clients to understand energy tariffs and try to reduce their energy consumption and carbon footprint by using energy efficient products and methods. Core tasks and competencies: energy efficiency. Supplementary skills: inform on government funding; electricity market; provide information on wind turbines; sales strategies; provide information on solar panels.

Occupation: fisheries adviser. Fisheries advisers provide consultancy on fish stocks and their habitats. They manage the costal fishing business modernisation and provide improvement solutions. Fisheries advisers develop plans and policies for fisheries management. They may provide advice on protected farms and wild fish stock. Core tasks and competencies: support fishery training procedures; fish biology; assess site production potential; apply fishery biology to fishery management; conduct research before survey; fisheries legislation; prepare surveying report; estimate fishery status; process collected survey data; analyse business objectives. Supplementary skills: soil science; aquaculture industry; wildlife; interpret scientific data to assess water quality; conduct underwater surveys.

Occupation: green ICT consultant. Green ICT consultants advise organisations on their green ICT strategy and its implementation in the most effective and efficient manner to allow the organisation to reach their short, mid, and long term ICT environmental objectives. Core tasks and competencies: apply business acumen; optimise choice of ICT solution; ICT environmental policies; define technical requirements; create project specifications; provide ICT consulting advice; promote environmental awareness; consult with business clients; manage environmental impact of operations; ensure compliance with environmental legislation. Supplementary skills: ICT sales methodologies; track key performance indicators; legal requirements of ICT products; hardware components suppliers; ICT market.

Occupation: energy engineer. Energy engineers design new, efficient and clean ways to produce, transform, and distribute energy to improve environmental sustainability and energy efficiency. They extract energy through natural resources, such as oil or gas, or renewable and sustainable sources, such as wind or solar power.  Core tasks and competencies: engineering principles; perform scientific research; adjust engineering designs; energy; technical drawings; engineering processes; energy market; use technical drawing software; approve engineering design. Supplementary skills: develop energy saving concepts; coordinate electricity generation; electricity; promote sustainable energy; ensure compliance with safety legislation.

Occupation: environmental expert. Environmental experts search for technological solutions to tackle environmental problems. They detect and analyse environmental issues and develop new technological production processes to counter these problematic issues. They research the effect of their technological innovations and present their findings in scientific reports. Core tasks and competencies: report pollution incidents; environmental legislation; advise on environmental remediation; advise on pollution prevention; carry out environmental audits; develop environmental policy; perform environmental investigations; investigate pollution; collect samples for analysis; environmental threats. Supplementary skills: promote environmental awareness; liaise with engineers; work with chemicals; apply scientific methods; environmental engineering.

Occupation: aquaculture environmental analyst. Aquaculture environmental analysts assess, plan and implement programmes to recognise, monitor and control environmental factors that can potentially affect the health of aquatic animals and plants. Core tasks and competencies: grow cultures used in monitoring experiments; measure the impact of specific aquaculture activity; apply standard feeding and nutrition protocols; pollution prevention; carry out training in environmental matters; perform environmental investigations; fish biology; assess contamination; develop environmental policy; environmental policy. Supplementary skills: provide training; communicate verbal instructions; speak different languages; communicate in English in a competent way; develop outreach training plans.

Occupation: energy manager. Energy managers coordinate the energy use in an organisation, and aim to implement policies for increased sustainability, and minimisation of cost and environmental impact. They monitor the energy demands 
and use, and develop improvement strategies, as well as researching the most beneficial source of energy for the organisation's needs. Core tasks and competencies: compose energy performance contracts; adhere to organisational guidelines; electrical power safety regulations; manage supplies; promote sustainable management; strive for company growth; liaise with managers; advise on heating systems energy efficiency; carry out energy management of facilities; manage budgets. Supplementary skills: renewable energy technologies; zero-energy building design; monitor utility equipment; identify faults in utility meters; energy market.

Occupation: bodyguard. Bodyguards offer protection to their clients against injury, attacks and harassment. They accompany individuals such as politicians and actors to various events and gatherings. Bodyguards observe the surrounding environment, anticipate threats and respond to security emergencies. They may carry and use guns. Core tasks and competencies: stay alert; execute inspection walkway; detain offenders; secure premises; adapt to changing situations; security threats; protect important clients; communicate with customers; handle conflicts; manage major incidents. Supplementary skills: provide protective escort; operate radio equipment; assist police investigations; assist emergency services; apply advanced driving techniques.

Occupation: chief data officer. Chief data officers manage companies' enterprise-wide data administration and data mining functions. They ensure data are used as a strategic business asset at the executive level and implement and support a more collaborative and aligned information management infrastructure for the benefit of the organisation at large. Core tasks and competencies: utilise decision support system; define data quality criteria; apply information security policies; manage ICT data classification; data storage; decision support systems; manage data; visual presentation techniques; information structure; manage ICT data architecture. Supplementary skills: database; IBM Informix; DB2; integrate ICT data; information architecture.

Occupation: railway infrastructure inspector. Railway infrastructure inspectors are responsible for checking the conditions of railways. They monitor compliance to health and safety standards and inspect the infrastructure to detect damage or flaws. They analyse and report on their findings to ensure railway conditions are maintained at a safe level. Core tasks and competencies: identify hazards in the workplace; ensure safe operation of railway during repairs; health and safety measures in transportation; conduct environmental surveys; quality assurance procedures; enforce railway safety regulations; write inspection reports; undertake inspections; perform inspection analysis; comply with legal regulations. Supplementary skills: provide railway technical advice; manage maintenance operations; ensure public safety and security; liaise with government officials; rail construction engineering.

Occupation: forestry inspector. Forestry inspectors monitor forestry operations to ensure that workers and their activities comply with proper legislation and standards. They perform inspections to examine operations, wages, costs and health and safety measures. Forestry inspectors also analyse and report on their findings. Core tasks and competencies: analyse business processes; enforce sanitation procedures; environmental legislation in agriculture and forestry; communicate health and safety measures; write work-related reports; monitor work site; undertake inspections; conduct environmental surveys; ensure compliance with legal requirements; maintain forest inventory. Supplementary skills: carry out forestry related measurements; forest conservation; check payment; review meteorological forecast data; conduct reforestation surveys.

occupation_family: MASCO 41/42 (Clerical Support - High Automation Risk in MY)
text: Occupation: office clerk. Office clerks are responsible for performing clerical and administrative duties in an office setting and support of business operations within a department. They assist all the administrative staff, secretaries, and assistants by sorting mail, filing forms and documents, answering phones, greeting clients, scheduling meetings, and serving drinks. Core tasks and competencies: route correspondence to business departments; fill out forms; use office systems; handle delivered packages; file documents; align content with form; use different communication channels; prepare correspondence for customers; process commissioned instructions; communicate by telephone. Supplementary skills: use software for data preservation; use microsoft office; process customer orders; perform cleaning duties; ensure proper document management.

Occupation: administrative assistant. Administrative assistants perform administrative and office support for supervisors. They perform a variety of tasks, such as answering telephone calls, receiving and directing visitors, ordering office supplies, maintaining the office facilities running smoothly, and ensuring that equipment and appliances work properly. Core tasks and competencies: handle mail; maintain statutory books; keep task records; use office systems; disseminate internal communications; company policies; perform business research; organise business documents; draft corporate emails; disseminate general corporate information. Supplementary skills: fix meetings; speak different languages; organise travel arrangements for staff; prepare presentation material; handle petty cash.

Occupation: podiatry assistant. Podiatry assistants help the podiatrist by carrying out supportive tasks such as assisting in diagnosing and treating the disorders, diseases and deformities of the feet, advising people on foot care techniques and the importance of foot care for promoting better mobility and general well-being. They also perform small tasks such as cutting toe nails, applying plasters and general clerical duties. Core tasks and competencies: recommend orthotic devices; ensure safety of healthcare users; comply with quality standards related to healthcare practice; communicate effectively in healthcare; orthopaedic conditions; administrative tasks in a medical environment; develop a collaborative therapeutic relationship; orthopaedics; follow clinical guidelines; respond to changing situations in health care. Supplementary skills: conduct podiatry consultation; medical terminology; employ foreign languages in care; work in a multicultural environment in health care; obtain healthcare user's medical status information.

Occupation: medical laboratory assistant. Medical laboratory assistants work under supervision of the biomedical scientist and carry out basic laboratory procedures. They work in the pre-analytical handling of samples such as checking the details of specimens received for analysis, maintaining analysers, loading reagents, and packaging specimens. They also perform clerical tasks such as monitoring the stock levels of reagents used in analysis. Core tasks and competencies: techniques of blood-sampling; apply safety procedures in laboratory; mix chemicals; work safely with chemicals; perform laboratory tests; prepare samples for testing; laboratory techniques; communicate effectively in healthcare; check the received biological samples; blood type classification. Supplementary skills: work with chemicals; collect biological samples from patients; data protection; interpret medical results; clinical biochemistry.

occupation_family: MASCO 41/42 (Clerical Support - High Automation Risk in MY)
text: Occupation: typist. Typists operate computers to type and revise documents and compile material to be typed, such as correspondence, reports, statistical tables, forms, and audios. They read instructions accompanying material or follow verbal instructions to determine requirements such as number of copies needed, priority and desired format. Core tasks and competencies: use free typing techniques; company policies; draft corporate emails; decode handwritten texts; align content with form; use microsoft office; use dictionaries; type error-free documents; transcription methods; apply grammar and spelling rules. Supplementary skills: write meeting reports; content development processes; translate keywords into full texts; integrate content into output media; stenography.

text: Occupation: auditing clerk. Auditing clerks collect and examine financial data, such as inventory transactions, for organisations and companies and ensure they are accurate, properly maintained, and that they add up. They review the numbers in databases and documents, evaluate, and consult and assist the source of the transaction if necessary, which includes accountants, managers or other clerks. Core tasks and competencies: conduct financial audits; liaise with managers; communicate problems to senior colleagues; audit techniques; fill out forms; write work-related reports; build business relationships; perform clerical duties; follow verbal instructions; prepare audit activities. Supplementary skills: enforce financial policies; carry out inventory control accuracy; interpret financial statements; accounting department processes; trace financial transactions.

Occupation: statistical assistant. Statistical assistants collect data and use statistical formulas to execute statistical studies and create reports. They create charts, graphs and surveys. Core tasks and competencies: statistics; apply scientific methods; write work-related reports; write technical reports; think analytically; apply statistical analysis techniques; identify statistical patterns; execute analytical mathematical calculations; perform data analysis; conduct quantitative research. Supplementary skills: carry out statistical forecasts; conduct public surveys; scientific research methodology; conduct financial surveys; perform clerical duties.

Occupation: legal administrative assistant. 
Legal administrative assistants carry out the daily administrative activities of firms, offices of notaries public, and companies. They perform activities such as writing mails, phone-answering and typing/keyboarding. They combine these activities with specific knowledge and understanding of the procedures and codes managed in legal business affairs. Core tasks and competencies: meet deadlines for preparing legal cases; procedural law; perform office routine activities; legal terminology; legal department processes; communicate by telephone; observe confidentiality; perform clerical duties; manage personnel agenda; compile legal documents. Supplementary skills: civil process order; revise legal documents; legal research; fix meetings; translate keywords into full texts.

Occupation: customer service representative. Customer service representatives handle complaints and are responsible for maintaining overall goodwill between an organisation and its customers. They manage data regarding customer satisfaction and report it. Core tasks and competencies: determine charges for customer services; customer service; control of expenses; have computer literacy; communicate with customers; process order forms with customer's information; provide information; perform escalation procedure; process customer orders; implement customer follow-up. Supplementary skills: upsell products; show diplomacy; perform data analysis; sales activities; speak different languages.

Occupation: client relations manager. 
Client relations managers act as the middle person between a company and its customers. They ensure that the customers are satisfied by providing them with guidance and explanation on their accounts and services received by the company. They also have possible other tasks such as developing plans or delivering proposals. Core tasks and competencies: identify customer's needs; develop professional network; liaise with managers; identify new business opportunities; create solutions to problems; build business relationships; analyse consumer buying trends; follow company standards; maximise sales revenues; public relations. Supplementary skills: contact customers; implement sales strategies; handle customer complaints; train employees; customer relationship management.

Occupation: railway passenger service agent. Railway passenger service agents spend time with railway station customers, answer their questions and react quickly and safely to unexpected situations. They provide information, mobility assistance, and security in railway stations. They provide accurate and up to date information on train arrival and departure times, train connections, and help customers plan their travels. Core tasks and competencies: maintain updated professional knowledge; write work-related reports; listen actively; identify customer's needs; think proactively; interpret customer non-verbal communication; deliver a sales pitch; manage the customer experience; product range of railway companies; deliver outstanding service. Supplementary skills: have computer literacy; show confidence; use microsoft office; act reliably; use positive language.

text: Occupation: customer contact centre information clerk. Customer contact centre information clerks provide information to customers via the telephone and other media such as email. They answer inquiries about a company's or oganisation's services, products and policies. Core tasks and competencies: perform customer management; provide customer follow-up; collect customer data; guarantee customer satisfaction; customer insight; keep records of customer interaction; answer incoming calls; communicate with customers; communicate by telephone; establish customer rapport. Supplementary skills: customer relationship management; handle helpdesk problems; improve customer interaction; call-centre technologies; provide customers with order information.

Occupation: after-sales service technician. After-sales service technicians provide after-sales service support to customers, such as the installation, maintenance and repair of the sold products. They take corrective actions to ensure customers’ satisfaction, resolve technical product-related issues and write customer summary reports. Core tasks and competencies: maintenance and repair; execute after sales activities; communicate with customers; contact customers; guarantee customer satisfaction; characteristics of services; implement customer follow-up; customer relationship management; customer service; product comprehension. Supplementary skills: apply technical communication skills; maintain relationship with customers; address problems critically; consumer protection; listen actively.

Occupation: ICT help desk manager. ICT help desk managers monitor the delivery of technical support services to clients according to the predefined deadlines.  They plan and organise the user support actions and troubleshoot ICT problems and issues. ICT help desk managers supervise the help desk team ensuring that the customers get the appropriate feedback and support. They also participate in developing customer service guidelines and in reinforcing the team. Core tasks and competencies: characteristics of products; characteristics of services; educate on data confidentiality; organisational structure; communicate with customers; manage staff; use ICT ticketing system; analyse staff capacity; secure sensitive customer's information; provide ICT support. Supplementary skills: perform project management; ICT help platforms; use customer relationship management software; ICT market; train employees.

Occupation: audiology technician. Audiology technicians create and service hearing aids and hearing protection products. They dispense, fit and provide hearing aids for those who need them. Core tasks and competencies: health, safety and hygiene legislation; order supplies for audiology services; produce impressions for ear moulds; perform repairs for hearing aids; advise customers on hearing aids; maintain laboratory equipment; hygiene in a health care setting; types of audiological equipment; perform technical tasks with great care; maintain records of clients' prescriptions. Supplementary skills: communication related to hearing impairment; adapt hearing tests; physiology of hearing; recommend hearing aids; assist audiologists with screening.

Occupation: desktop publisher. Desktop publishers are responsible for the layout of publications. They use computer software to arrange texts, photographs and other materials in a pleasing and readable finished product. Core tasks and competencies: multimedia systems; search databases; align content with form; graphic design; desktop publishing; printing techniques; ICT software specifications; adapt to type of media; follow work schedule; adapt to artists' creative demands. Supplementary skills: perform image editing; grammar; proofread text; consult with editor; perform backups.

Occupation: metallurgical manager. Metallurgical managers coordinate and implement short and medium term metallurgical or steel-making production schedules, and coordinate the development, support and improvement of steel-making processes, and the reliability efforts of the maintenance and engineering departments. They also partner with ongoing remediation initiatives. Core tasks and competencies: improve business processes; cost management; types of metal manufacturing processes; follow company standards; legal requirements of ICT products; conduct metallurgical structural analysis; deal with pressure from unexpected circumstances; engineering processes; forecast organisational risks; ensure compliance with environmental legislation. Supplementary skills: manage staff; maintain relationship with customers; design metal components; physics; chemistry.

Occupation: process engineer. Process engineers apply engineering concepts in order to improve all kinds of production and manufacturing processes in terms of efficiency and productivity. They evaluate the variables and constraints present in given processes and present engineering solutions to optimise them. Core tasks and competencies: project management; manage engineering project; analyse production processes for improvement; engineering principles; perform scientific research; manufacturing processes; interpret technical requirements; use technical drawing software; troubleshoot; engineering processes. Supplementary skills: read engineering drawings; develop test procedures; manage budgets; adjust engineering designs; perform project management.

Occupation: business intelligence manager. Business intelligence managers gain knowledge of the industry, the innovative processes therein, and contrast them with the operations of the company in order to improve them. They focus their analysis in the supply chain processes, warehouses, storage, and sales as to facilitate communication and revenue improvement. Core tasks and competencies: organisational policies; ensure compliance with policies; manage project metrics; develop company strategies; interpret business information; corporate social responsibility; liaise with managers; develop revenue generation strategies; advise on efficiency improvements; business management principles. Supplementary skills: project management; business intelligence; supply chain management; perform business research; train employees.

Occupation: human resources manager. Human resources managers plan, design and implement processes related to the human capital of companies. They develop programs for recruiting, interviewing, and selecting employees based on a previous assessment of the profile and skills required in the company. Moreover, they manage compensation and development programs for the company's employees comprising trainings, skill assessment and yearly evaluations, promotion, expat programs, and general assurance of the well-being of the employees in the workplace. Core tasks and competencies: human resource management; plan medium to long term objectives; evaluate training; develop employee retention programs; identify with the company's goals; manage budgets; employment law; organise staff assessment; develop training programmes; comply with legal regulations. Supplementary skills: evaluate performance of organisational collaborators; calculate benefits; assessment processes; actuarial science; company policies.

Occupation: human resources officer. Human resources officers develop and implement strategies that help their employers select and retain appropriately qualified staff within that business sector. They recruit staff, prepare job advertisements, interview and short-list people, negotiate with employment agencies, and set up working conditions. Human resources officers also administer the payroll, review salaries and advise on remuneration benefits and employment law. They arrange for training opportunities to enhance employees' performance. Core tasks and competencies: develop professional network; employment law; identify with the company's goals; manage payroll; listen actively; assess character; recruit employees; profile people; use communication techniques; labour legislation. Supplementary skills: negotiate with employment agencies; monitor company policy; evaluate training; apply social media marketing; mentor individual employees.

Occupation: human resources assistant. Human resources assistants provide support in all the processes and efforts carried by human resources managers. They help in the preparation of recruitment processes by scanning CVs and narrowing the selection to the most suitable candidates. They perform administrative tasks, prepare communications and letters, and perform the tabulation of the surveys and assessments carried out by the department. Core tasks and competencies: identify with the company's goals; maintain professional administration; manage payroll reports; administer appointments; observe confidentiality; job market offers; listen actively; fix meetings; apply company policies; support managers. Supplementary skills: human resources department processes; recruit employees; assist employee health programmes; advertising techniques; coach employees.

Occupation: natural resources consultant. Natural resources consultant provide advice on the protection and management of natural resources, namely fauna, flora, soil and water to companies and governments which exploit these resources. They strive to guide companies on an appropriate policy for exploiting natural resources in industrial contexts, raise awareness on health issues, and ensure the conservation of ecosystems for sustainable interventions in natural habitats. Core tasks and competencies: conduct ecological research; advise on nature conservation; advise on environmental remediation; ensure compliance with environmental legislation; develop environmental policy; assess environmental impact; monitor nature conservation; analyse ecological data; natural areas maintenance; conserve natural resources. Supplementary skills: manage forests; botany; environmental legislation; administer treatments to fish; ecology.

Occupation: operations manager. Operations managers plan, oversee and coordinate the daily operations of production of goods and provision of services. They also formulate and implement company policies and plan the use of human resources and materials. Core tasks and competencies: manage supplies; follow company standards; establish daily priorities; ensure equipment availability; plan health and safety procedures; ensure equipment maintenance; strive for company growth; manage staff; manage logistics; manage budgets. Supplementary skills: meet deadlines; create a financial report; inspect industrial equipment; manufacturing processes; oversee planning of security systems.

Occupation: mine manager. Mine managers control, direct, plan and coordinate mining production activities. They have statutory responsibility for safety and are also responsible for environmental impact. They oversee the acquisition, installation, maintenance and storage of mining plant and equipment. They lead and manage according to the organisation's code of conduct. Core tasks and competencies: manage emergency procedures; mine safety legislation; impact of geological factors on mining operations; interface with anti-mining lobbyists; supervise staff; develop health and safety strategies in mining; assess operating cost; deal with pressure from unexpected circumstances; show social competences; electricity. Supplementary skills: prepare technical reports; health and safety hazards underground; mechanical engineering; electrical engineering; geology.

Occupation: financial markets back office administrator. Financial markets back office administrators perform administrative tasks for all the transactions registered in the trading room. They process transactions involving securities, derivatives, foreign exchange, commodities, and manage the clearing and settling of trades. Core tasks and competencies: handle financial transactions; manage administrative systems; customer service; electronic communication; banking activities; financial markets; financial products; maintain records of financial transactions. Supplementary skills: international commercial transactions rules; trade foreign currencies; securities; foreign valuta; economics.

Occupation: metal production manager. Metal production managers organise and manage the day-to-day and long-term project work in a metal fabrication factory, to process basic metals into fabricated metals. They create and schedule production plans, recruit new staff, enforce safety and company policies, and strive for customer satisfaction through guaranteeing the product's quality.\
 Core tasks and competencies: liaise with managers; optimise financial performance; use IT tools; follow company standards; manage commercial risks; develop manufacturing policies; implement strategic planning; adhere to organisational guidelines; types of metal; meet deadlines. Supplementary skills: plan shifts of employees; manage discarded products; apply control process statistical methods; perform market research; negotiate supplier arrangements.

Occupation: product manager. Product development managers are responsible for managing the lifecycle of a product. They research and develop new products in addition to managing existing ones through market research and strategic planning. Product managers perform marketing and planning activities to increase profits. Core tasks and competencies: combine business technology with user experience; analyse consumer buying trends; oversee quality control; develop communication strategies; analyse market financial trends; develop new products; identify market niches; execute marketing plan; develop promotional tools; perform market research. Supplementary skills: manage feedback; maximise sales revenues; analyse cultural trends; sales strategies; manage profitability.

Occupation: banking products manager. Banking products managers study the market of banking products and adapt the existing ones to the characteristics of this evolution or create new products to suit clients needs. They monitor and evaluate the performance indicators of these products and suggest improvements. Banking products managers assist with the sales and marketing strategy of the bank. Core tasks and competencies: follow company standards; market research; financial products; analyse market financial trends; coordinate marketing plan actions; plan health and safety procedures; sales strategies; strive for company growth; liaise with managers; financial analysis. Supplementary skills: communicate with banking professionals; carry out strategic research; make strategic business decisions; survey techniques; statistics.

Occupation: tourism product manager. Tourism product managers analyse the market, research potential offers, develop products, plan and organise the distribution and marketing processes. Core tasks and competencies: sales strategies; carry out inventory planning; implement marketing strategies; manage production of destination promotional materials; plan medium to long term objectives; produce content for tourism brochures; set up pricing strategies; manage contracts; manage distribution channels; maintain customer service. Supplementary skills: apply foreign languages in tourism; utilise cross-selling.

Occupation: footwear product development manager. Footwear product development managers coordinate the footwear design and the product and collection development process in order to comply with design specifications, deadlines, strategic requirements and policies of the company. They track style development and review design specification in order to meet the design vision, the manufacturing environment, and the company’s financial goals. Core tasks and competencies: footwear manufacturing technology; apply development process to footwear design; perform market research in footwear; create solutions to problems; implement footwear marketing plan; work in textile manufacturing teams; develop footwear and leather goods marketing plans; reduce environmental impact of footwear manufacturing; distinguish fabrics; make technical drawings of fashion pieces. Supplementary skills: create technical sketches for footwear; create 3D CAD footwear prototypes; operate 2D CAD for footwear pattern engineering; ergonomics in footwear and leather goods design; use CAD for lasts.
